The defendant, Joshua Oladipupo, was arraigned on Friday at the Iyaganku Magistrates’ Court, Ibadan, on a three-count charge bordering on publication of fake news and conduct likely to cause a breach of the peace. He pleaded not guilty to the charges. The presiding magistrate, Mrs Oluwabusayo Osho, granted him bail in the sum of N2 million with two sureties. The court directed that the sureties must be close blood relations of the defendant and own landed properties within the court’s jurisdiction. It further stipulated that the properties must have Certificates of Occupancy and survey documents. Pending the fulfilment of the bail conditions, the magistrate ordered that Oladipupo be remanded at the Agodi Correctional Centre. A News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) report on Monday said the defendant was still in custody as he had yet to perfect his bail. The prosecutor, Inspector Adeshina Folaranmi, told the court that the alleged offences were committed in October 2026 in the Dugbe area of Ibadan. Folaranmi alleged that Oladipupo published false information on Facebook and other social media platforms, claiming that the late singer’s personal assistant, Babadunni Gbolabo, his wife, Damilola, and members of his maternal family were responsible for his death. He further alleged that the publications were intended to cause fear and alarm among members of the public. The prosecutor said the offences contravened Sections 59 and 249(d) of the Criminal Laws of Oyo State, 2000. The court adjourned the case until December 17, 2026, for hearing. Toluwanisings, whose real name was Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, died on October 14, 2026, and was buried at his residence in Ibadan on November 9 following a disagreement among family members over his final resting place.
